status: exact affine scale-localization and unified local Vaughan reduction with one open signed gate

rows.statement: For 0<alpha<1 set q_n=mu(n)n^(-1-alpha), r_N=sum_(n>N)q_n, and R_alpha=sum_(N>=1)N^alpha|r_N|^2.
rows.proof_boundary: These are the reciprocal-Mobius tail coordinates from Lemmas 11.22T-X.

rows.statement: For dyadic K, u_K:=sum_(N=K)^(2K-1)r_N=sqrt(K)c_(K,0).
rows.proof_boundary: The affine mean coefficient is exactly one dyadic block sum of the tail sequence.

rows.statement: u_K=sum_n q_n w_K(n), where w_K(n)=min((n-K)_+,K).
rows.proof_boundary: Count the block tails containing q_n; w_K is constant for n>=2K.

rows.statement: M_alpha=sum_(K dyadic)K^(alpha-1)|u_K|^2.
rows.proof_boundary: This is Lemma 11.22X.15 after u_K=sqrt(K)c_(K,0).

rows.statement: Define v_K:=u_K-(1/2)u_(2K).
rows.proof_boundary: The coefficient 1/2 is forced by cancellation of the two constant kernel plateaux beyond 4K.

rows.statement: Define W_K(n)=n-K for K<n<=2K, W_K(n)=(4K-n)/2 for 2K<n<4K, and W_K(n)=0 otherwise.
rows.proof_boundary: W_K is a nonnegative compact tent with maximum K.

rows.statement: v_K=sum_(K<n<4K)mu(n)n^(-1-alpha)W_K(n).
rows.proof_boundary: This follows from W_K=w_K-(1/2)w_(2K); the infinite tail cancels exactly.

rows.statement: Put p=(alpha-1)/2, d_K=K^p u_K, and e_K=K^p v_K.
rows.proof_boundary: Then M_alpha=sum_K|d_K|^2 and the filtered affine energy is E_aff=sum_K|e_K|^2.

rows.statement: Let rho_alpha=2^(-(1+alpha)/2), so 0<rho_alpha<1.
rows.proof_boundary: The strict contraction is uniform over the dyadic scale index for fixed alpha.

rows.statement: e_K=d_K-rho_alpha*d_(2K).
rows.proof_boundary: Use rho_alpha*2^p=1/2.

rows.statement: The coefficient envelope gives |d_K|=O_alpha(K^((1-alpha)/2)) and hence rho_alpha^m d_(2^m K)=O_alpha(2^(-alpha*m)).
rows.proof_boundary: This supplies the boundary condition needed to invert the forward scale filter without assuming the target energy.

rows.statement: d_K=sum_(m>=0)rho_alpha^m e_(2^m K).
rows.proof_boundary: Iterate row 10 and use the boundary decay in row 11.
The upper bound is the shift triangle inequality; the lower bound follows from the geometric-series inverse.

rows.statement: M_alpha<infinity iff E_aff:=sum_(K dyadic)|e_K|^2<infinity.
rows.proof_boundary: The infinite affine mean kernel has therefore been replaced by compact tent tests without estimating it.

rows.statement: |e_K|^2=D_aff,K+2C_aff,K, where D_aff,K=K^(alpha-1)sum_n mu(n)^2 n^(-2-2alpha)W_K(n)^2 and C_aff,K is the corresponding sum over K<n<m<4K.
rows.proof_boundary: This is the diagonal/off-diagonal expansion of the compact tent square.

rows.statement: 0<=D_aff,K<=3K^(-alpha), so sum_(K dyadic)D_aff,K<infinity.
rows.proof_boundary: There are fewer than 3K terms, W_K<=K, and n>K.

rows.statement: M_alpha<infinity iff sup_J sum_(K<=2^J)C_aff,K<infinity.
rows.proof_boundary: Use rows 14-16 and monotonicity of the partial filtered affine energies.

rows.statement: Let E_br,K=K^(-2-alpha)||[S_K]||_K^2, where S_(K,m)=M(K+m)-M(K) and [.] is the quotient modulo constants.
rows.proof_boundary: The sum of E_br,K is L_alpha from Lemma 11.22X.

rows.statement: E_br,K=D_br,K+2C_br,K, with D_br,K=K^(-2-alpha)Delta_K and C_br,K=K^(-2-alpha)C_K.
rows.proof_boundary: Delta_K and C_K are the Brownian-bridge diagonal and off-diagonal terms from Lemma 11.22X.

rows.statement: 0<=D_br,K<=K^(-alpha)/6.
rows.proof_boundary: Use Delta_K<=(K^2-1)/6.

rows.statement: Define E_loc=sum_(K dyadic)(|e_K|^2+E_br,K).
rows.proof_boundary: Rows 14 and 18 give R_alpha<infinity iff E_loc<infinity.

rows.statement: For h>=1 define G_(K,h)(n) as K^(alpha-1)[n(n+h)]^(-1-alpha)W_K(n)W_K(n+h) on K<n<n+h<4K, plus K^(-3-alpha)(n-K)(2K-n-h) on K<n<n+h<2K.
rows.proof_boundary: The first summand is the affine tent kernel and the second is the normalized Brownian-bridge kernel.

rows.statement: G_(K,h)(n)=0 unless K<n<n+h<4K.
rows.proof_boundary: Both formerly separate open components are now local on at most two adjacent dyadic annuli.
The tent product contributes at most K^(-1-alpha); the bridge product contributes at most K^(-1-alpha)/4.

rows.statement: E_loc(J)=D_loc(J)+2O_loc(J), where O_loc(J)=sum_(K<=2^J)sum_h sum_n mu(n)mu(n+h)G_(K,h)(n).
rows.proof_boundary: Combine rows 15 and 19 before taking a cutoff limit.

rows.statement: The per-scale unified diagonal is at most (19/6)K^(-alpha), hence D_loc(infinity)<infinity.
rows.proof_boundary: Add the bounds 3K^(-alpha) and K^(-alpha)/6.

rows.statement: R_alpha<infinity iff sup_J O_loc(J)<infinity.
rows.proof_boundary: The partial local energies are nonnegative and monotone, and their diagonal converges.

rows.statement: Split each n-sum in O_loc into K<n<=2K and 2K<n<4K.
rows.proof_boundary: This places every compact test into the standard (X,2X] form with X=K or X=2K.

rows.statement: Green and Tao, Lemma 4.1, supply the finite Vaughan Type I/II identity on each interval (X,2X].
rows.proof_boundary: Only the exact divisor identity is imported; no estimate for the endogenous shifted-Mobius tests is attributed to it.

rows.statement: For interval a in {0,1}, define g_(K,h,a)(n)=mu(n+h)G_(K,h)(n) restricted to (2^a K,2^(a+1)K].
rows.proof_boundary: Summing mu(n)g_(K,h,a)(n) over h and a recovers the unified off-diagonal O_loc scale by scale.

rows.statement: With the standard finite Vaughan coefficients on each interval, O_loc,K=-TI_loc,K+TII_loc,K.
rows.proof_boundary: Apply the identity termwise in h and in the two interval pieces, then retain the signed difference.

rows.statement: R_alpha<infinity iff sup_J sum_(K<=2^J)(-TI_loc,K+TII_loc,K)<infinity.
rows.proof_boundary: This is one compact signed Type I/II target for both the affine mean and centered bridge.

rows.statement: Replacing -TI_loc,K+TII_loc,K by the sum of separate absolute values is not an equivalent reduction.
rows.proof_boundary: There are O(K^2) shift/base pairs of amplitude O(K^(-1-alpha)), giving the divergent scale K^(1-alpha).

rows.statement: The natural averaged-Chowla o(K^2) pair scale becomes only o(K^(1-alpha)) after the normalized kernel, one full power above the diagonal K^(-alpha) calibration.
rows.proof_boundary: This is a power audit of the published averaged theorem, not a lower bound on the actual unified correlation.

rows.statement: The invertible scale filter localizes M_alpha but supplies no Mobius cancellation estimate.
rows.proof_boundary: Compact support must not be reported as a Type I/II gain, a full Burnol bound, or a proof of RH.

rows.statement: The Abel/low-DCT commutator is not a remaining obligation: the centered quotient handles nonconstant modes and the scale filter handles the affine mean.
rows.proof_boundary: Future work should attack the unified signed kernel rather than reintroduce the retired commutator.

rows.statement: Arbitrary finite coefficient tests verify the tail count, tent cancellation, normalized filter, inverse truncations, and norm bounds; Mobius tests verify both signed expansions and the two-interval Vaughan residual.
rows.proof_boundary: Finite validation checks the algebra only and is not asymptotic evidence for the open signed estimate.

rows.statement: Let T_(K,m)=sum_(i=1)^m q_(K+i), 0<=m<K, and retain the weighted centered energy K^alpha||[T_K]||_K^2.
rows.proof_boundary: Together with the affine mean this is the exact DCT decomposition before transfer to ordinary Mertens increments.

rows.statement: Define Z_K=Kq_(2K)+sum_(2K<n<4K)(4K-n)q_n/2; then v_K=sum_(i=1)^(K-1)i*q_(K+i)+Z_K.
rows.proof_boundary: The q_(2K) endpoint belongs to the affine tent and not to the length-K centered path.

rows.statement: For 1<=i,j<K, K^(alpha-1)ij+K^alpha[min(i,j)-ij/K]=K^alpha min(i,j).
rows.proof_boundary: The affine rank-one square exactly restores the constant direction removed by the Brownian bridge.

rows.statement: |e_K|^2+K^alpha||[T_K]||_K^2=K^alpha sum_(t=1)^K|Z_K/K+sum_(i=t)^(K-1)q_(K+i)|^2.
rows.proof_boundary: This is finite variance completion, including the terminal row t=K whose suffix sum is zero.

rows.statement: R_alpha<infinity iff sum_(K dyadic)K^alpha sum_(t=1)^K|Z_K/K+sum_(i=t)^(K-1)q_(K+i)|^2<infinity.
rows.proof_boundary: Use dyadic tail-energy comparison, DCT Parseval, and the invertible affine scale filter.

rows.statement: Every row in the positive criterion uses only q_n with K<n<4K.
rows.proof_boundary: The Cholesky form is compact and nonnegative but does not bound its own Mobius suffix sums.

rows.statement: Put s=1+alpha, z_K=Z_K/K, and beta_K=(2K)^s*z_K; then beta_K=mu(2K)+sum_(2K<n<4K)((2K)/n)^s(4K-n)/(2K)*mu(n).
rows.proof_boundary: This is one explicit compact future anchor, not an unproved short-interval cancellation estimate.

rows.statement: Every coefficient of mu(n) in beta_K lies in [0,1] and the support is 2K<=n<4K.
rows.proof_boundary: Coefficient boundedness gives only the trivial |beta_K|=O(K); it does not itself close the criterion.

rows.statement: With a_i=(K+i)^(-s) for i<K, a_K=(2K)^(-s), A_(K,t)=sum_(i=t)^K a_i*x_i and B_(K,t)=sum_(i=t)^K x_i, where x_K=beta_K, finite Abel summation gives mutually inverse triangular maps.
rows.proof_boundary: The terminal choice a_K*beta_K=z_K is essential; omitting the future anchor would break the exact inverse.
The constants follow from explicit row/column sums for the Abel matrix and its inverse and are uniform for 0<alpha<1.

rows.statement: R_alpha<infinity iff sum_(K dyadic)K^(-2-alpha)sum_(t=1)^K|beta_K+sum_(i=t)^(K-1)mu(K+i)|^2<infinity.
rows.proof_boundary: This removes all power weights from the current-block suffixes while preserving one bounded-coefficient future anchor.

rows.statement: If H_K:=sum_(t=1)^K|beta_K+sum_(i=t)^(K-1)mu(K+i)|^2=O_epsilon(K^(2+epsilon)) for some epsilon<alpha, then the alpha criterion holds.
rows.proof_boundary: The coefficientwise estimate gives only H_K=O(K^3), which is one full power short of this calibration.

rows.statement: Matomaki and Teravainen prove o(H) cancellation for every interval of length H=x^theta when theta>0.55.
rows.proof_boundary: An o(H) pointwise bound has no fixed square-root-scale power and does not make the K-term suffix-square family summable.

rows.statement: Matomaki-Radziwill and the higher-uniformity short-interval theorems give strong cancellation outside small exceptional sets of base points.
rows.proof_boundary: The present endpoints are one fixed dyadic sequence; no source-backed de-averaging theorem excludes every one of those points from the exceptional sets.

rows.statement: All criteria are imposed separately for fixed alpha>0; the diagonal majorant is sum_(K dyadic)K^(-alpha).
rows.proof_boundary: At alpha=0 this majorant is not summable. Cofinality alpha_j->0 does not permit setting alpha=0 or demanding a uniform limit in alpha.

rows.statement: Prove the unified signed criterion in row 32 for every member of one fixed cofinal sequence alpha_j->0 without assuming RH.
rows.proof_boundary: No signed Type I/II power gain, full Burnol bound, RH, PF-infinity, or Lambda<=0 conclusion is supplied here.
